title: Layered Egress Fabric Terraform module for resilient subnet & endpoint routing
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Build a composable Terraform module that implements a zone-aware, layered egress fabric for Private deployments. The module will provision subnet tiers, NAT/IGW placement and failover choreography, VPC interface and gateway endpoints, and a route reconciliation layer that enforces guardrails and automatic healing. Goal: provide a single reusable module for customers and internal on-prem installers that reduces misconfiguration, speeds safe upgrades, and exposes health probes so the operator can detect and auto-recover egress failures.
acceptance_criteria: Module supports defining public, private, and application-specific subnet tiers with per-tier route tables and explicit NAT/IGW attachments
Zone-aware NAT gateway placement with optional autoscaling (replaceable with managed NAT gateways) and a deterministic failover ordering
Native support for VPC endpoints: aws_vpc_endpoint (gateway) and aws_vpc_endpoint_service (interface) provisioning via variables and per-subnet placement rules
Route reconciler that detects drift against declared topology and emits planned diffs and optional automated apply with an audit trail
Built-in health checks: synthetic egress probes (to S3/metadata/health-endpoints), NAT/IGW latency/packet-loss thresholds, and automated alerting hooks
Documented upgrade path: in-place module upgrade steps, canary plan, and rollback plan with minimal traffic disruption
Integration tests using terratest/bats that run in CI and exercise destroyed/recreate scenarios across 3 AZs
implementation_notes: Module will be split into submodules: subnets, egress (nat/igw), endpoints, routing-reconciler, and health-probes
Prefer terraform 1.5+ and use lifecycle rules to avoid accidental replacement of customer-controlled resources
Use tagging conventions (redwood:env, redwood:owner, redwood:role) for observability and cost allocation
Provide optional lazy-created managed EC2 autoscaled NAT fleet for environments that disallow managed NAT gateways due to cost
Routing reconciler implemented as a lightweight controller (Lambda + Dynamo) or optional external operator — initial POC as scheduled reconciliation Lambda
Health probes will be implemented as Lambda/CloudWatch Synthetics that emit metrics to the Console and expose a short TTL KPI for autoscaling triggers
test_plan: CI: terratest suite that provisions module in a temporary account (3 AZs), validates connectivity to S3/health URL, then tears down
Chaos test: simulate AZ failure by removing route and ensure failover ordering preserves outbound connectivity
Upgrade test: run terraform plan/apply against a stable deployment to validate in-place changes without NAT replacement
Security test: verify endpoint policies, PCA usage for interface endpoints, and that default route propagation does not leak across peered VPCs
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: Ticket created with initial scope and acceptance criteria (Aisha)
2025-02-18: Module scaffolding merged (PR #842). Added submodule layout and initial variables (Luca)
2025-02-21: Design review with Networking & Security teams. Feedback: make default endpoint policy deny-by-default and require explicit allow lists for customer-managed endpoints (Security)

2025-02-25: POC reconciler implemented as scheduled Lambda that compares declared routes vs. actual. Observed race when routes are updated by another automation; added optimistic locking via Dynamo (Luca)

2025-02-28: Performance note — managed NAT gateway creation time varies by region (6–10 minutes). Decided to add optional prewarm step for Dedicated installs to avoid cold path on first rollout (Decision by Aisha + Infra)
2025-03-03: Integration tests added to CI; one flaky test found around IGW propagation during apply. Created follow-up ENG-483900 to harden apply ordering and lifecycle hooks
review_feedback: Security: enforce least-privilege IAM for the reconciler and grant only Describe/Modify routes on the target VPC
Networking: prefer explicit route table attachments per subnet instead of relying on default route propagation to avoid surprises with peering
DX: add example module usage in README with both minimal and enterprise configurations and a quickstart that uses local backend for dev
Observability: emit reconciliation diffs and health probe summaries as structured logs to simplify Console ingestion
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Automatic route apply might overwrite manual operator changes. Mitigation: reconciler can run in 'report-only' mode and requires an explicit opt-in variable to auto-apply; all auto-applies produce an audit log
Risk: Managed NAT costs for large deployments. Mitigation: provide an alternative EC2-based NAT fleet and guidance in README comparing cost/latency trade-offs
Risk: Endpoint policy misconfiguration could expose telemetry endpoints. Mitigation: default DENY policy on new endpoint resources and explicit allowlist variable with validation
next_steps: Finish health probe metric mapping to Console metrics pipeline (owners: Observability team)
Land reconciler retry/backoff fixes and retry-idempotency (owner: Luca)
Add terraform import examples and migration guide for customers using older module versions
Schedule security review for 2025-03-10 and tag compliance checklist
notes: This ticket aims to unify several prior ad-hoc terraform scripts into a single opinionated module that is safe for both hosted Dedicated installs and customer-managed private deployments. Keep interface small and well-documented; avoid provider-specific hacks in top-level module.
